texts.preamble: Raushan Sharma (Dar) vs Sandeep Kumar (210/18, Ppp) on 20 February, 2024 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No: 539/2019 Raushan Kumar Sharma vs. Sandeep Kumar Raushan Kumar Sharma S/o Sh. Rajender Singh R/o H.No. 259, Ward no. 10 Bheem Basti, Old Faridabad, Haryana ....Driver/R-1 2. Xchange Leasing India Pvt. Ltd. Plot no. 300, ground floor, Sector 29, Gurgoan, Haryana ....Owner/R2 3. Park, E-25, Sector 62, Noida, U.P ....Insurance company/R-3 :2: Date of Accident : 13.03.2018 Date of filing of Dar : 10.07.2019 Date of decision : 20.02.2024 Raushan Sharma (Dar) vs Sandeep Kumar (210/18, Ppp) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130983598/ 1 Award 1. The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (Dar), filed by the police on 10.07.2019, in terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act and the same is treated as a claim petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2.
texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are that on 27.08.2018, a written complaint was received by ASI Jamaluddin (IO), in which it was informed that on 13.03.2018, claimant /petitioner /injured Amod Sharma had returned to Delhi from Bihar. He boarded a bus no. 433 (plying on route from New Delhi to Badarpur), for Lal Quan. After being dropped at Lal Quan bus stand, when he was crossing the road with his wife and minor son Roshan Kumar, at about 12:00 PM, vehicle no. HR-55Y-4360 came at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit minor son (aged about 13 years) of the claimant from behind. Due to the impact, minor Roshan Kumar fell on the road. Driver of the offending vehicle took minor Roshan Kumar to the Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital and got him admitted there. He assured to reimburse the medical expenses of his treatment, however, failed to do so. 3. On complaint, an FIR no. 210/2018 was registered at PS :3: Pul Prahladpur u/s 279/337 of IPC and the matter was investigated. It is pursuant to the investigation that a charge sheet u/s 279/337 of IPC was filed before Ld. MM and a DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Pursuant to notice issued to the respondents, respondents (including driver, owner of the offending vehicle and Insurance company with which such vehicle was insured) appeared and filed written statement. As per reply filed by the Insurance company/Respondent no. 3 the FIR has been lodged after a delay of more than 5 months of such alleged accident. It has been pleaded that there seems to be a collusion between the claimant and the owner and driver of the alleged offending vehicle. It has further been pleaded that there is no MLC as on date of accident and the hospital where the victim was apparently taken for treatment is much far from the place of incident. It is pleaded that the fact that the victim was not taken to a nearby hospital such as AIIMS or Safdarjung hospital, raises doubt in the claim. It is further pleaded that the offending vehicle has also been referred as a bus in the charge sheet while such vehicle was infact a Maruti Ritz commercial car. The variation in the description of vehicle raises doubt in the claim. Raushan Sharma (Dar) vs Sandeep Kumar (210/18, Ppp) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130983598/ 2 The owner of the vehicle/Respondent no. 2 also filed a reply denying the claim of occurrence of the accident or involvement of vehicle no. HR-55Y-4360 or rash and negligent driving by its driver. 5. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 13.08.2019. OPP 3. Relief. 6. Thereafter, evidence was led by the petitioner by examining complainant Sh. Amod Kumar Sharma (father of the injured) as PW-1. 10. In the present case, petitioner (father of injured minor) has specifically deposed that on 13.03.2018 he had come to New Delhi from Bihar along with his wife and son (victim Raushan Kumar) and boarded bus no. 433 to Lal Quan. When petitioner deboarded the bus and was crossing the road, Respondent no. 1 driving vehicle no. HR-55Y-4360 came at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit son of the petitioner. Son of the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained injuries in his right leg. At that time, Respondent no.1 took the injured to Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital and assured to bear expenses of his treatment. PW1 further deposed that it Raushan Sharma (Dar) vs Sandeep Kumar (210/18, Ppp) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130983598/ 3 is therefore that he did not make any complaint or call at 100 number. It is deposed that Respondent no. 1 did not render any financial help and since petitioner is unable to bear the hardship of the treatment of his son, he made a complaint to the police on 28.03.2018, PS Pul Prahladpur.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. It is deposed that the son of the petitioner also suffered a fracture in his right leg and has been unable to recover completely. It is deposed that son of the petitioner is still undergoing treatment. It is further deposed that the petitioner has expended Rs. 3,00,000/- on the medical treatment of his son by taking loan however, the bills of treatment have been misplaced. 11. It is further seen that as per the FIR, the offending vehicle has been described as 'Gaadi' by the complainant. It is in fact the IO who has wrongly referred to it as 'bus'. 12. It has been contended by the respondents that the accident did not occur and that the details of the offending vehicle have been planted subsequently. Cross examination of PW1 reveals that though he admitted to have not made a police complaint or a call on 100 number instantly, he justified to have not done so in expectations of being reimbursed by the driver of such offending vehicle. It is also a stand persistently taken by the petitioner that it was the driver of the offending vehicle himself, who took the injured to the hospital and assured to bear the expenses. In such circumstances, where the petitioner has categorically stated the number of the offending vehicle and reasonably explained the reason for the delay, his claim cannot be doubted merely for the reason of delaying lodging of the FIR. Reliance is placed on the observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ravi vs. Badrinarayan & ors., (Civil appeal no. 196/2011, arising out of SLP (C) No. 11974 of 2008, decided on 18.02.2011): "20. 13. It has further been pleaded by the respondents that the claim is doubtful as not only there is a delay in FIR but also that the injured was allegedly admitted in Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya hospital despite the fact that AIIMS and Safdarjung Hospital were much closer to the alleged spot of incident. Hence, merely for the reason that many other hospitals fall on the way or were closer to the spot of incident, does not raise a ground to doubt the genuineness of the claim, particularly Raushan Sharma (Dar) vs Sandeep Kumar (210/18, Ppp) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130983598/ 4 when the injury sustained by the minor was not of the nature or fatal to compel him to approach the nearest hospital. 14. Further, petitioner has relied upon a photocopy of an emergency/casualty registration card of Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital to prove that his son had been medically examined and treated at such hospital. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 18. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 21. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. 24. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 29. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. In the case of semi-illiterate claimants, the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, Raushan Sharma (Dar) vs Sandeep Kumar (210/18, Ppp) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130983598/ 10
